newsitem.title: JAPAN: Police suspect Japan firm sent toxicants to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Police suspect Japan firm sent toxicants to N.Korea.

text.p: Police on Tuesday raided the offices of a small Japanese trading firm suspected of illegally exporting toxic chemicals that could be used to make weapons to North Korea.

Police in Kobe, western Japan, said investigators suspected Osaka-based Sowa Boeki exported 41 tonnes of mercury and four tonnes of phenol to communist North Korea last year without proper government approval.
The export value of the toxic material was about 30 million yen ($247,000), a Kobe police spokesman said.
Officials of Sowa Boeki could not be reach for comment.
Phenol can be used to make gunpowder and dioxin-based defoliants, including Agent Orange that was used by the U.S. military during the Vietnam War.
Mercury is a key ingredient in night-vision devices such as infra-red sensors for guns.

The Kobe police spokesman quoted company president Yoshimitsu Aobuchi as saying his firm sold the toxic chemicals to North Korea but was not aware of a law that requires toxic-substance exporters to get prior government approval.

In a separate case last April, an employee of a Kobe-based trading house was arrested for illegally exporting to North Korea hydrofluoric acid and sodium fluoride -- two key ingredients of the deadly nerve gas sarin.

Members of the doomsday cult Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) are on trial for a sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway in March 1995 which killed 12 people and made some 6,000 others ill. ($=121 yen)
